eventIdentity.freshEvent: AP-NORC published a new US poll measuring concern about AI's environmental effects and views about local data-centre limits, electricity, water and clean-energy requirements.
eventIdentity.distinctFromPublished: The published EPA story explains a proposed change to public participation in data-centre planning. This candidate measures current US public opinion about AI and data-centre impacts. It does not report another permit rule or a measured environmental effect.
notClaimed: No claim that the poll proves data centres caused a specific environmental harm.
No claim that support for a policy means it has been enacted.
No claim that all data centres are primarily for AI.

readerContract.reader: Adult beginners hearing arguments about AI infrastructure, including residents near proposed data centres.
readerContract.humanQuestion: What does this poll actually say people are worried about, and what does it not tell me about a project near me?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Separate public concern and policy preferences from measured local water, electricity or environmental effects.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: A poll measures what people think; a project record measures what a particular facility is expected to use or change.

evidence.sourceRole: Complete AP report and methodology note
evidence.limits: Polling reports views and stated policy preferences; it is not direct environmental measurement.
Same publisher/study family; not independent corroboration and shares the AP aggregate budget.

boundedFacts: 53% of US adults said they were extremely or very concerned about AI's environmental impact, up from 41% in the prior-year poll.
About six in ten supported limiting new data centres; about two thirds supported clean-energy requirements.
The poll used 3,424 adult respondents from July 6-24, 2026 and reports a plus or minus 2.2 percentage-point sampling error.
The sample combined a probability-based panel with opt-in online panels and used NORC calibration intended to address potential nonprobability-sample bias.

sourceBudgetContract.draftingRequirement: Allocate every AP-derived visible phrase before producer qualification. Say percentage points, not percent, for the 53 versus 41 comparison.

limits: Keep AI-environment and local-data-centre questions separate.
State the hybrid sampling method and margin of sampling error in beginner language.
Do not imply that polling error captures every possible source of survey bias.
Use a distinct primary project record before making claims about any named local facility.
Treat policy support as opinion, not law or implementation.
nextProducerSteps: Editorially decide whether the poll offers enough practical reader payoff beyond the published EPA participation story.
If proceeding, recover the specific AP-NORC questionnaire/topline or methodology report through a normal legitimate route and bind it as the same poll family.
Complete the teaching producer contract, exact source-word allocation, live Library binding, visual admission and qualified independent review before any public candidate.
notDone: No public prose, art, queue, issue, source cursor or coverage mutation.
No claim of independent corroboration beyond the AP-NORC study family.
